subject: Prefetch + Batched Inference: PoC cost validation & close timeline
messages:
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@nexahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Prefetch/batch assumptions for our PoC cost model

Soojin — thanks again for the demo last week. We walked through the integration with our engineering lead yesterday and we want to validate a couple of cost assumptions before we sign the PoC MSA.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm expected tokens per request: we expect ~120 tokens inbound (user prompt) and ~480 tokens avg generation.
- Cache/prefetch behavior: we plan to prefetch symptom-context for ~30% of requests (reusable prompts), curious what cache hit rate you see in similar healthcare workloads.
- Batching: We expect bursts up to 60 RPS for short periods; what's a realistic batching profile to keep 95th latency under 400ms?

If you can share a version of your cost model with those knobs (tokens/$, cache hit, batching latency tradeoffs) we can run it through our procurement and engineering checks. I attached our internal traffic profile.

Thanks — want to close this in the next two weeks if numbers line up.

—Alex
Alex Dunn
Head of Integrations, NexaHealth
alex.dunn@nexahealth.com
Attachment: nexa_poc_traffic_profile.csv (csv)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prefetch/batch assumptions for our PoC cost model

Alex — appreciate the detail, and great to hear the team is moving fast. I attached a PoC cost workbook (nexa_poc_cost_model_v3.xlsx) and a small cache-hit profile we generated from a comparable 30% prefetch workload (cache_hit_profile.json). High-level notes below and an ask for one quick confirm so we can finalize the MAP: 

Highlights from our model (defaults applied):
- Tokens per call: request 120 / response 480 (configurable).
- Baseline quantization: q8_0 recommended for this model family; reduces serving $/token by ~35% vs fp16 in our tests.
- Cache hit assumptions: 30% prefetch gives effective token reduction of ~18% (depends on repeated prompt shapes).
- Batching: with continuous batching enabled, a 60 RPS burst with 50ms batching window keeps 95th latency ~360ms on a c5g cluster equivalent; if you need <200ms we recommend dedicated pools or stricter per-request routing.

Immediate asks for the MAP:
1) Can you confirm you accept q8_0 by default for the PoC (yes/no)?
2) Target 95th latency SLO for patient-facing flows (we proposed 400ms).

If you confirm those two items we’ll update the MAP with mutual milestones, gating criteria (token/$ acceptance threshold, cache hit verification), and a proposed close timeline. I set a tentative close date 2027-04-12 in the workbook.

Attached: nexa_poc_cost_model_v3.xlsx (xls/xlsx), cache_hit_profile.json (json)

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

On Tue, Mar 30, 2027 at 08:20 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Ben/Marissa — looping you in to validate the technical knobs in the attached model.
> 
> Please review the cost tab and the latency/batching sheet in nexa_poc_cost_model_v3.xlsx. Specific asks: 
> - Ben: can you confirm the 50ms batching window / continuous batching number and whether 360ms 95th is realistic on our standard Dedicated pool?
> - Ben: how much extra savings do we see with KV prefix caching at 30% hit (ballpark % reduction in tokens/$)?

Quick answers below. I ran a short sim against our perf harness with the provided traffic profile and the assumptions in the workbook.
- 50ms batching window + continuous batching: realistic. On a 3x T4 dedicated pool the 95th is ~340–380ms depending on request variance. If Nexa requires consistent <250ms we should propose a single-model pinned pool or 1.5x capacity.
- q8_0 savings: ~32–38% ops cost reduction vs fp16 on this model family (matches Soojin's sheet).
- KV prefix caching at 30% hit: expect ~12–20% reduction in total served tokens depending on how many prefetched tokens are in the response payload (their 30% prefetch -> our 18% estimate is conservative).

Gating recommendation for MAP:
- Acceptance threshold: tokens/$ must be <= $0.45 per 1k inference tokens under PoC traffic (workbook shows $0.41 with q8_0 + 30% cache hit).
- Measurement: run two 48-hour smoke windows against Prod-mirroring; verify observed cache hit >= 25% and 95th latency <= 400ms.
- Timeline: if Nexa confirms q8_0 and SLO=400ms by EOD tomorrow, we can sign MAP and hit close by 2027-04-12.

I attached my short sim output to the workbook (see "perf_sim_notes" tab). If Marissa is good with the q8_0 default commercial line, I think we can finalize.

—Ben
